correctness.rationale: Dirichlet plus CRT constructs arbitrarily large primes isolated throughout a prescribed finite ±H window in either unit class ±1 mod m. If A is product-minimal of product M, appending isolated q>s(A) preserves product minimality: any competing product <=qM has smaller-factor product T<4M^2, forcing its largest prime b into the excluded window around q and hence b=q. Starting from singleton 2 or 3 and appending t−1 isolated primes of classes ±1 programs every sum residue: 2j variation covers odd moduli, and the two seed parities cover even moduli, for t>=m+1. Vinogradov supplies a second representation of each sufficiently large offset as at most four distinct primes. Prime-prefix exchange Lemma 5 compares any inserted large primes against removed small primes: the gap G>11M forces product ratio v(U)/v(V)>M via sorted exchange and (a−1)!e^(−a)>=2e^(−3)>1/11. Thus maximum product omits exactly A (K=pi(x)−t), while a four-prime offset produces at least pi(x)−4 summands (L−K>=t−4>=R). Prime gaps of arbitrarily prescribed finite length in a suitable progression are unbounded by CRT-Dirichlet. Infinite sequence of different prefix sums completes the argument. Independently verified residue programming across m<=300 and key factorial inequality; finite checks do not substitute for Dirichlet/Vinogradov or the exchange proof.

value.rationale: Extending a natural globally unbounded partition discrepancy to every congruence class removes all congruence obstructions, including non-coprime classes, with common-cardinality programmable offset witnesses. The universal modular quantifiers are a nontrivial strengthening relevant to additive prime partitions, not an arbitrary residue sample. No density, least witness or effective upper bound is asserted.

final_claim: For all moduli m>=1, residues c mod m (including nonunit classes), and R>=1, infinitely many n congruent to c satisfy L(n)-K(n)>=R, where L maximizes the number of distinct-prime summands and K counts the summands in the unique maximum-product exact-sum distinct-prime partition.
limitations: No density or effective bound for least n in a class; infinitely many n only.
Incomplete primary text access is a priority limitation, not mathematical disproof.
